questions.question: Today ________ are seen as personal accessory - portable, powerful and simple to operate.
questions.solution:
Today computers are seen as a personal accessory - portable, powerful and simple to operate.

 
• A computer is an electronic device that is instructed to process numerical as well as non-numerical operations automatically through computer programming.
 
• It was designed by British mathematician Charles Babbage between 1833 and 1871.
 
• They are used as control systems for a large variety of industrial and consumer devices.

questions.question: The boundaries of the plates of the earth's _________ are the weak zones known as seismic or fault zones.
questions.solution:
The boundaries of the plates of the earth's crust are the weak zones known as seismic or fault zones

 
• The boundaries of the earth's plate are the weak zones. Here earthquakes are more likely to occur. These weak zones are called seismic or fault zones.
 
• Seismic or fault zones of India: In India, the most of the threatened areas are:
 
 
• Kashmir
 
• Western and central Himalayas
 
• The whole of North-East
 
• Rann of Kutch
 
• Indo-Gangetic Plane.
 
• Some areas of south India.

questions.question: The gravitational force of attraction between two bodies is ________ the distance between the two bodies.

options.text: Directly proportional to the square of
Inversely proportional to the square of

questions.solution:
__CONCEPT__:

__
 
• Law of Universal Gravitation: It states that all objects attract each other with a force that is proportional to the masses of two objects and inversely proportional to the square of the distance that separates their centres.
 
• It is given mathematically as follows:

F = (Gm₁m₂)/(R²)

Where m1 and m2 are the mass of two objects, G is the gravitational constant and R is the distance between their centres.

EXPLANATION__:

__
 
• The gravitational force of attraction between two bodies is inversely proportional to the square of the distance between the two bodies.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• From the universal law of gravitation,
 
 
• The force is attractive in nature.
 
• The distance between the two objects is their centre-to-centre distance, and hence the force acts along the line joining the centres. Therefore, it is a central force.
 
 
 
• Non-contact force is a force that acts on an object without being in contact with the object. Since gravitational force acts without each body being in contact with another body, it is a non-contact force.

questions.question: Find the acceleration (in m/s²) of a body which accelerates from 15 m/s to 40 m/s in 2 seconds.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **12.5**

__**EXPLANATION:**__

 
• The acceleration of a body that accelerates from 15 m/s to 40 m/s in 2 seconds is 12.5 m/s².
 
• Initial velocity = 15m/s and Final velocity = 40m/s.
 
• So net velocity = 40 ‐15(m/s) which is equal to 25m/s.
 
• Now formula for acceleration= net velocity/time
 
• Therefore here, acceleration = 25/2 = 12.5 m/s².

questions.question: As per the guidelines issued by the RBI in September 2017, all Peer-to-Peer lending (P2P) platforms will be treated as ________.
questions.solution:
As per the guidelines issued by the RBI in September 2017, all Peer-to-Peer lending (P2P) platforms will be treated as NBFCs.

questions.question: Which country has developed world’s first artificial intelligence politician named SAM?
questions.solution:
New Zealand has developed world’s first artificial intelligence politician named SAM.

 
• This virtual politician was created by Nick Gerritsen, a 49-year-old entrepreneur in New Zealand.
 
• It can answer a person’s queries regarding local issues such as policies around housing, education, and immigration.

questions.question: In October 2017, the biggest ever highway project was launched in India. It aims to develop approximately how many kilometers of roads by the year 2022?
questions.solution:
In October 2017, the biggest ever highway project was launched in India. It aims to develop approximately 83,000 kilometers of roads by the year 2022.

 
• A cost of about Rs. 7 lakh crore will be spent in this project.
 
• The plan also involves constructing of bridges, highways, and green-field expressways.
 
• It is aimed at pushing economic activity and generating at least 14.2 crore man-days across the country over the next five years. 
 
• The programme includes the Bharatmala scheme, under which 34,800 km of highways would be constructed at the cost of Rs. 5.35 lakh crore.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a feature found in almost every cell?
questions.solution:
The cell wall is NOT a feature found in almost every cell.

 
• The cell wall is a rigid layer of polysaccharides lying outside the plasma membrane of the cells of plants, fungi, and bacteria.
 
• In the algae and higher plants, it consists mainly of cellulose.
 
• It provides the cell with both structural support and protection.
 
• It also acts as a filtering mechanism.
 
• A major function of the cell wall is to act as pressure vessels to prevent over-expansion of the cell when water enters.

questions.question: Some amount of plasma, proteins, and blood cells escape through the pores present in the walls of capillaries into the intercellular spaces in the tissue and form _________.
questions.solution:
Some amount of plasma, proteins and blood cells escape through the pores present in the walls of capillaries into the intercellular spaces in the tissue and form Lymph.

 
• The lymph is a medium of circulation in the human body like the blood.
 
• But lymph flows only in one direction, i.e. from the body tissues to the heart. 
 
• Functions of the lymph are:
 
 
• Transport's nutrients.
 
• Bring CO2 wastes from tissue fluid to blood.
 
• Protects the body from infection.

questions.question: Under which Article of Indian Constitution an emergency can be declared on the grounds of war, or external aggression or armed rebellion?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option __**2**__ i.e. __**Article 352**__

 
• Under **Article 352** of the **Indian Constitution** an emergency can be declared on the grounds of war, or external aggression or armed rebellion.
 
• **Article 352** says that if the President is satisfied that a serious emergency exists in which the security of the country or any part of it is threatened by war or external aggression or armed rebellion, he may proclaim an emergency.
 
• **The President** **cannot proclaim a war** **emergency** unless the Union cabinet gives him in writing that such proclamation should be made.

questions.question: The constitution of India refers to the budget as the ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option __**1**__ i.e. __**Annual Financial Statement.**__

 
• **The constitution of India** refers to the budget as the **Annual Financial Statement.**
 
• **The budget** is a statement of the estimated expenditure and receipts of the Union Government in a financial year.
 
• **Provisions of the Budget** are mentioned in **Article 112.**

questions.question:
Saturated carbon compounds can form which types of chain structures?

I. Straight chain

II. Branched-chain
questions.solution:
Saturated carbon compounds can form Straight and Branched types of chain structures.

 
• Saturated hydrocarbons are hydrocarbons that contain only single bonds between carbon atoms.
 
• Each carbon atom is bonded to as many hydrogen atoms as possible.

questions.question:
An atom can achieve octet by ______.

I. Sharing electron

II. Gaining electron

III. Losing electron
questions.solution:
An atom can achieve octet by Sharing electron, Gaining electron and Losing electron.

 
• Octet rule: It says that atoms gain, lose, or share electrons with other atoms in order to fill their valence level with eight electrons.
 
• Electron loss or gain is entirely dependent on the atom concerned with it.
 
• Example:
 
 
• Fluorine tries to complete its Octet by gaining an Electron.
 
• Sodium tries to complete its Octet by losing an Electron.

questions.question: Which of the following range is known as 'Sahyadri'?
questions.solution:
The Western Ghats are also known as 'Sahyadri'.

 
• They run in the north-south direction forming the western edge of the Deccan Plateau.
 
• They are about 1600km in extent, from the Tapi Valley in the North to almost Kanyakumari in the South.

questions.question: Where is located the most active volcano in the world?
questions.solution:
The most active volcano in the world is located around the Pacific Ocean.

 
• Currently, Kilauea is the world’s most active volcano, located in Hawaii.
 
• There are about 1500 active volcanoes in the world, most of which are located around Pacific Rim, known as Ring of Fire.
 
• Ring of Fire includes South American and North American plates, the Bougainville, Mariana Islands, New Zealand, Tonga, and the Philippines, Japan, Indonesia, etc.

questions.question: The term "Smart Money" broadly refers to ________.
questions.solution:
The term “Smart Money” broadly refers to credit cards.

 
• Credit cards allow us to borrow money from the credit provider to pay for something without using your cash or savings in a bank account.
 
• There's a limit to borrow money (called credit limit) and one has to pay it back.
